vulns.title: signed pack message omits coin type enabling cross coin signature replay
vulns.root_cause: sell_pack<COIN> authorizes a payout of `amount` from a `Game<COIN>` reserve by verifying a server ed25519 signature over a `PackMessage { pack_id, amount, nonce }`. The function is generic over the coin type `COIN`, but the signed payload does NOT include `COIN` (or the specific game/reserve id) — the message binds only pack_id, amount, and nonce. So a signature the server issues to authorize a sale of a CHEAP coin is byte-for-byte identical to what would authorize the same pack_id/amount/nonce for a VALUABLE coin: the attacker takes a legitimately-obtained signature for `sell_pack<CheapCoin>` and replays it against `sell_pack<ValuableCoin>` (same shared `Server` key across all coin games), passing the signature check and draining the most valuable reserve. The generic type parameter is unbound to the authorization. The fix is to include the coin type (e.g. `type_name::get<COIN>()`) — and ideally the game object id — in the signed message so a signature is valid only for the exact coin/reserve it was issued for.
